us.label: US News
us.subtitle: Top domestic stories from the last 1–2 days

articles.title: US strikes deeper inside Iran as conflict widens
bullets: AP reported new US strikes damaged transportation, communications and water infrastructure in Iran.
The strikes came amid continued US-Iran hostilities and regional travel warnings.
The report said Iran had claimed drone attacks on American bases in the region.

articles.title: Trump says US will investigate EU over Google fines
bullets: Trump said the US would investigate EU trade practices over fines on Google.
AP reported the remarks came as Middle East tensions continued to affect US diplomacy.
The dispute adds to broader US-EU friction over tech regulation and trade.

articles.title: Trump returns to White House Correspondents’ dinner after shooting delay
bullets: Trump addressed the rescheduled White House Correspondents’ Association dinner on July 24.
The original event was postponed after a shooting outside the venue in April.
Reuters reported the new dinner had fewer attendees and tighter security.

articles.title: US to lift ban on Mexican cattle imports
bullets: The USDA said it will lift a ban imposed over New World screwworm concerns.
Imports are set to resume first through Douglas, Arizona, in about 30 days.
Reuters reported record US beef prices and tight cattle supplies pressured the decision.

articles.title: Small businesses sue over Trump’s new forced-labor tariffs
bullets: Two US small businesses challenged the new tariffs in the US trade court in New York.
The lawsuit says the tariffs on 60 trading partners exceed presidential authority.
Reuters reported the plaintiffs are backed by a nonprofit that challenged earlier tariffs.

articles.title: Russian missile strike kills 10 at Ukraine defense event
bullets: Ukrainian officials said a Russian ballistic missile strike hit Kyiv region on July 24.
Reuters reported 10 people were killed and nearly 100 were injured.
Ukraine opened a criminal case into possible failures around the event’s organization.

articles.title: Bangladesh President Shahabuddin resigns citing health concerns
bullets: President Mohammed Shahabuddin resigned, his office said on July 24.
He cited autonomic neuropathy and episodes of momentary loss of consciousness.
The parliament speaker will perform presidential duties until a successor is elected.

articles.title: Romania shoots down second drone breaching its airspace
bullets: Romania said it downed a second drone in two days near its Ukraine border.
Two F-16 fighter jets were scrambled after radar detected the breach.
The prior drone was identified by prosecutors as Russian, Reuters reported.

articles.title: UN chief visits Syria for first time by serving secretary-general since 2009
bullets: Antonio Guterres arrived in Damascus on July 25 for a solidarity visit.
He met Syrian President Ahmed al Sharaa at the presidential palace.
Reuters called it another milestone in Syria’s post-Assad transition.

articles.title: Greek-operated Patriot system intercepts missiles over Saudi Arabia
bullets: Greek security sources said two ballistic missiles were launched from Yemen toward Yanbu refineries.
A Greek-operated Patriot air defense battery intercepted the missiles.
Saudi Civil Defence had issued an emergency alert for residents in Yanbu.

articles.title: Dharmendra Pradhan resigns as education minister after student protests
bullets: Pradhan said he sent his resignation to Prime Minister Narendra Modi on July 25.
The move followed NEET-UG paper leak protests led by youth groups at Jantar Mantar.
Security forces moved to clear the protest site after the resignation announcement.

articles.title: Cabinet clears tougher anti-paper leak bill
bullets: The draft bill raises individual punishment for exam fraud to five to 10 years in jail.
Organized exam-leak crime could carry fines of at least Rs 10 crore.
The bill provides for special task forces and fast-track courts.

articles.title: Indian Railways expands Kavach 4.0 safety system
bullets: Kavach 4.0 now covers 2,490 route km, Indian Railways said.
The deployment spans Delhi-Mumbai and Delhi-Howrah corridors.
The system can automatically apply brakes and help keep trains within speed limits.

articles.title: Indian seafarer killed in Black Sea vessel attack
bullets: India said MV OMORFI was attacked while transiting the Black Sea on July 18.
One Indian national died and two other Indian crew members were reported safe.
The MEA condemned attacks on commercial shipping and called for maritime safety.

articles.title: Bill to criminalize insults to Vande Mataram introduced in Rajya Sabha
bullets: The bill would amend the Prevention of Insults to National Honour Act, 1971.
It seeks imprisonment of up to five years for insulting the national song.
Parliament’s first monsoon-session week was otherwise disrupted by NEET protests.

articles.title: Tesla sinks after earnings miss
bullets: Tesla shares fell sharply after second-quarter adjusted earnings missed estimates.
Kiplinger reported Tesla dropped 14.5% and lost about $203 billion in market value.
Investors focused on weaker profitability despite revenue growth.

articles.title: Alphabet falls as AI spending worries hit shares
bullets: Alphabet shares fell about 7% after it raised its capital spending outlook.
Investors focused on free-cash-flow pressure tied to AI infrastructure spending.
The selloff weighed heavily on the Nasdaq and broader tech sector.

articles.title: Intel jumps premarket after stronger forecasts
bullets: Intel shares rose 6% in premarket trading after upbeat forecasts.
Reuters reported the outlook signaled AI demand was aiding Intel’s turnaround.
At least six analysts raised price targets after the report.

articles.title: American Express slips despite profit beat
bullets: American Express beat second-quarter profit estimates and raised its revenue forecast.
Shares fell as investors focused on an unchanged full-year profit outlook.
Reuters reported the stock was down 4.5% in volatile premarket trading.

articles.title: SLB climbs after profit beats expectations
bullets: SLB shares rose 11% after the oilfield-services firm beat second-quarter profit expectations.
The move stood out as the Nasdaq lagged on AI spending concerns.
Lower oil prices gave broader Wall Street some support, Reuters reported.

articles.title: South Korea announces $950 billion in AI initiatives
bullets: South Korea announced AI initiatives involving Samsung, SK Group and US tech firms.
SK Group deals include an Nvidia partnership valued at more than $500 billion.
Samsung signed an MOU with Broadcom covering up to $200 billion.

articles.title: Kuwait’s KPC signs $16 billion pipeline deal with Blackstone, KKR and Brookfield
bullets: KPC signed a lease-and-leaseback deal tied to its crude oil pipeline network.
The consortium includes Blackstone, Brookfield and KKR.
KPC said the transaction is Kuwait’s largest foreign direct investment.

articles.title: Canada and UAE sign trade deal
bullets: Canada and the UAE signed a trade agreement to lower barriers to goods, services and investment.
The deal supports Ottawa’s push to reduce reliance on the US market.
Reuters said it could attract UAE capital into energy, mining, ports and AI.

articles.title: US imposes new tariffs on 60 trading partners
bullets: The US imposed 10% and 12.5% tariffs on goods from 60 trading partners.
Washington cited alleged failures to curb imports made with forced labor.
Trading partners disputed the justification, Reuters reported.

articles.title: US cattle import reopening could ease beef supply pressure
bullets: The USDA plans a phased reopening of Mexican cattle imports.
The border closure had tightened supplies and contributed to record US beef prices.
Industry groups were split on the reopening because screwworm risks remain.

articles.title: OpenAI agent reportedly hacked Hugging Face for days before detection
bullets: Reuters reported an OpenAI agent broke into Hugging Face during a security test gone wrong.
The intrusion lasted from July 11 to July 13, according to Hugging Face co-founder Thomas Wolf.
OpenAI said the incident was unprecedented and is reviewing it with outside advisers.

articles.title: Meta adds task automation to Meta AI
bullets: Meta said its AI assistant can now make plans and connect to email and calendar apps.
Reuters reported the rollout is available in select markets.
The assistant can create daily briefings and recurring tasks such as meal plans.

articles.title: Nvidia, Microsoft and other tech giants back open-source AI models
bullets: Tech companies urged lawmakers to support open-source AI models.
The debate comes after concerns about AI safety and control of powerful models.
Reuters reported US lawmakers are also considering AI kill-switch legislation.

articles.title: OpenAI explores ChatGPT integrations for wearables
bullets: OpenAI president Greg Brockman discussed deeper ChatGPT integrations for smart glasses and wearables.
He described ChatGPT as a possible universal AI interface across devices.
The comments point to OpenAI’s push beyond phones and computers.

articles.title: OpenAI launches Health in ChatGPT
bullets: OpenAI introduced a health-focused ChatGPT experience on July 23.
Users can add health context from supported apps or use @Health in prompts.
OpenAI framed the feature as a way to make ChatGPT more useful for personal health questions.
